`mentl query <file> "unreferenced"` answers, for every name the weave
declares, how many of its reference sites lie outside its own declaration.
Zero is the finding. It is the import read one altitude down and turned
around: that one asks whether any name an edge brings is referenced inside
the importing extent; this asks whether any site referencing a declared
name lies outside the declaring one. Same two columns, same O(1) probe.

Nine dead fns came out of src/ by hand one pin ago, one grep per name and
then reading each hit to tell a call from a mention in a comment.

Its first run found a bug in the graph, not a list of dead code. 461 of
4388 read unreferenced, and the roster was implausible: TStringLit at zero
refs, TIntLit at exactly two, both of them its construction sites in the
lexer. Every match on a constructor registered nothing. That resolution
has to happen — arity and exhaustiveness are checked against the very
scheme it finds — so the edge was proven and dropped. graph_ref_note now
fires at the PCon site above its env match, for infer_var_ref's own stated
reason: a missing constructor is still a reference. 461 -> 415.

What remains is mostly type names, and it is a different finding at a
different price. `fn f(y: Nonexistent)` yields E_TypeMismatch at the body:
the name is never resolved, so nothing was dropped and there is no edge to
carry. Banked as Hβ.infer.type-name-in-annotation-never-resolves with its
repro. One was a deletion; the other is a build.

convention" but $lexpr_consumes_no_stack returns 1 for tag 313 (LDeclareFn),
telling $ec5_emit_body NOT to drop residue. Net: 1 i32 leaked onto stack
per LDeclareFn in LBlock. With each handler-with-state having 1+ arms

entries no longer hid behind the (unreachable) polymorphism that the
pre-fix LUnresolved sentinels emitted. With proper `(call_indirect)`

tokensafe/c6398ca:
Three independent bugs compounded to make USDC score 75:

1. BigInt precision in top-holders: scale factor 10000n was too small for
   USDC's 9-quadrillion supply, truncating all holder percentages to 0%.
   Fixed by scaling to 1_000_000n (0.01% precision).

2. Token age returning ~0 hours: getSignaturesForAddress(limit: 10) returns
   10 most-recent txs, not oldest. For USDC with millions of txs, the
   "oldest" was seconds old → +10 penalty. Fixed by fetching 1000 sigs;
   if 1000 return, token is established → null age, no penalty.

3. No trusted mint authority mechanism + wrong freeze authority address:
   Circle legitimately holds both authorities on USDC (CCTP minting,
   regulatory compliance). Added TRUSTED_MINT_AUTHORITIES set with
   Circle's verified pubkey. Fixed freeze authority from ...JtsGMsNeDDw
   to ...NTQYwrRCrar (verified from mainnet getAccountInfo).

Additionally, context-aware penalty reduction for untrusted authorities:
tokens showing institutional maturity signals (deep liquidity, established
age, distributed holders) get reduced authority penalties instead of full
+30/+25. This catches legitimate tokens we haven't whitelisted yet.

150 tests passing (47 risk-score, 32 checks, 26 integration, 27 delta,
18 liquidity).
